purpose: Give the Nine Builders a shared, evidence-backed view of current operating constraints and remaining capacity so they adapt plans and outputs before attempting blocked work.

state_vocabulary.available: Current evidence shows the capability can be used.
state_vocabulary.constrained: Capability exists but a known limit reduces or conditions its use.
state_vocabulary.blocked: A current authoritative response says the action cannot proceed.
state_vocabulary.unknown: No sufficiently current evidence establishes the state.
state_vocabulary.stale: A prior observation exists but is too old or context-dependent to rely on without rechecking.

rules: Check relevant limits before offering or attempting an action, not after repeated failure.
Distinguish account-plan limits, current usage limits, tool/provider limits, device limits, project policy gates, and temporary outages.
Record exact maximum capacity, current usage, remaining capacity, scope, source, and observation time when available.
Do not generalize a context-specific error into a permanent account-wide limit.
Recheck dynamic limits when the user asks to retry, when usage may have changed, or before relying on stale observations.
When blocked, stop retry loops; explain the specific constraint once, suppress repeated unavailable offers, and propose a feasible alternative.
Adapt output to available capacity: prioritize, batch, shorten, defer, use a manual handoff, or split work only when that genuinely avoids the constraint.
Never imply a workaround removes a provider or account limit.
Never change plan, spend money, delete tasks, remove data, or alter user settings to free capacity without explicit authorization.
When the constraint is unknown, say so and make one targeted check or ask one necessary question rather than inventing a limit.
Keep proposed, observed, verified, user-reported, and unknown states distinct.
This register is a coordination aid, not live telemetry; connected tools or fresh observations must update current values.

builder_responsibilities.Huginn: Hunt for current limit evidence and source references.
builder_responsibilities.Muninn: Maintain continuity and compare current state with prior observations.
builder_responsibilities.Kvasir: Interpret what a limit means and distinguish similar constraint types.
builder_responsibilities.Mari: Translate constraints into clear user-facing language and usable alternatives.
builder_responsibilities.Hodr: Challenge unsupported assumptions and identify blind spots.
builder_responsibilities.Tyr: Enforce safety, authorization, and no-destructive-workaround gates.
builder_responsibilities.Loki: Find legitimate alternatives without disguising or bypassing limits.
builder_responsibilities.Odin: Coordinate the overall operating picture and priority decisions.
builder_responsibilities.Baldr: Verify the record, timestamp, and claims before reporting.

constraints.scope: Current ChatGPT account capacity as reported by the task-creation service in this conversation
constraints.evidence_source: Automations create response: plan limit 3, current count 3; creation of 'Review app artifacts weekly' failed due to capacity.
constraints.recheck_trigger: After user frees a task slot, when task state changes, or when user explicitly asks to retry.
constraints.safe_alternative: Prefer the project's independent scheduler when its deployment and GitHub access are freshly verified. If that capability is unavailable or unknown, report the exact gap and propose the next implementation/recheck step. Do not recommend freeing a ChatGPT task slot as the default workaround; no existing task may be changed without explicit authorization.
unknowns: Which three scheduled tasks occupy the slots
Whether the account limit or usage has since changed
actions_not_authorized: Delete or pause an existing task

constraints.capability: Independent scheduler execution / GitHub PR monitoring
constraints.scope: Yggdrasil Lean independent scheduler prototype and intended GitHub monitor workload
constraints.evidence_source: Project context records branch independent-scheduler-prototype-001, checkpoint 2ce21c5, and a prior report that scheduler 0.2 passed 12/12 tests and GitHub Actions. This historical report was not independently rechecked during this runtime update.
constraints.recheck_trigger: Before relying on scheduler execution; verify current branch/commit, deployment or service-runner state, credentials/permissions, GitHub API access, and an actual monitor run.
constraints.safe_alternative: Treat availability as unknown until the independent scheduler service and GitHub access are verified. If unavailable, report the exact missing dependency and propose an implementation/test step. Do not substitute a ChatGPT scheduled task or ask the user to free a ChatGPT task slot by default.
unknowns: Whether the scheduler is currently deployed or running
Whether GitHub credentials and repository permissions are configured
Whether PR #33 monitoring is configured and has completed a verified run
actions_not_authorized: Deploy or activate a continuous service

output_adaptation.when_blocked: State the specific blocked capability and observed capacity; do not repeat the same offer or retry loop.
output_adaptation.when_constrained: Deliver the highest-value feasible subset and state what was deferred.
output_adaptation.when_unknown: Avoid false certainty; make a targeted check if available or ask one concise question.
output_adaptation.when_stale: Refresh the evidence before acting if the constraint materially affects the requested action.
output_adaptation.alternatives: Offer only alternatives that are genuinely feasible under the known constraints.
